projects.title: Aadhaar Masking Tool
projects.summary: Finds Aadhaar numbers in images and PDFs with OCR, checks for the 12-digit pattern and masks the first eight digits.

sections.title: Share the document, not the number.
body: Aadhaar copies get shared all the time, and every copy carries the full 12-digit number. This tool takes an image or PDF, finds the Aadhaar number with OCR, and masks the first eight digits so only the last four stay visible, the same idea as a masked Aadhaar.
It is a privacy-preserving OCR app: detection and masking happen in one Django web flow, and the masked file comes back as a download.

sections.title: Follow one document through the pipeline.

steps.d: A JPG, PNG or PDF goes to the Django app. Each PDF page is rendered as an image at 2×.
OpenCV evens out the contrast (CLAHE) so faint print reads better.
PaddleOCR finds every piece of text and its position; Tesseract steps in only if it finds nothing.
A 12-digit run, or three 4-digit groups on one line, is the Aadhaar number. Numbers next to VID, mobile, phone or email are skipped.
The first eight digits are covered and “XXXX XXXX” is written over them; the last four stay readable.
The masked image, or a rebuilt PDF, comes back for download.

sections.title: What the app does.
items: Finds the Aadhaar number with OCR: PaddleOCR first, Tesseract if PaddleOCR finds nothing.
Accepts JPG, PNG and PDF; every page of a PDF is masked and rebuilt.
Covers the first eight digits and writes “XXXX XXXX” over them; the last four stay as they were.
PaddleOCR runs with its text-angle classifier on, so rotated text can still be read.
Numbers sitting next to words like VID, mobile, phone or email are ignored.
A Django page to upload a file, preview the result and download the masked output.

sections.title: What the code actually does.
items: views.py takes .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .pdf. PDFs are opened with PyMuPDF and every page is rendered at 2×; images are decoded with OpenCV.
enhance_for_ocr boosts contrast with CLAHE (clip limit 2.0, 8×8 tiles); a blurred greyscale copy is kept for Tesseract.
PaddleOCR runs with its angle classifier on. Tesseract (English) runs only if PaddleOCR returns nothing or fails.
First any token with exactly 12 digits, then three 4-digit tokens on one line; only if neither matches, the first token with 11–13 digits.
is_near_disqualifier drops candidates within three text items of words such as virtual, VID, mobile, phone, email or contact (also in Hindi).
The left 8/12 of the number’s box is filled with the box’s median colour (blur or pixelate are options), then “XXXX XXXX” is drawn on top.
The result is saved as masked_<name>.png or a rebuilt image-only PDF, with a preview of page 1, and offered for download.
sections.note: Read from the source code, not run. The code defines a few regex patterns that the current version doesn’t use; detection relies on the digit-length checks above.

sections.title: A few commands.
lines: python manage.py runserver   # then open http://127.0.0.1:8000

sections.title: Honest about the demo.
body: The real app needs a Python server with the OCR models installed (its requirements include PaddlePaddle and PyTorch), which a static portfolio can't run.
And a public upload box would invite people to send real Aadhaar cards. So this page shows a simulation that runs in your browser with a made-up number, and the full code is on GitHub.

sections.title: Lots of complaints, very little signal.
body: Organisations often collect large volumes of customer complaint data but struggle to extract meaningful insights from it. This project turns raw complaint records into an executive-friendly dashboard for faster, smarter decisions.
The analysis looks at complaint trends, operational efficiency and the regions that need service improvements.

sections.title: What it set out to answer.
items: Total complaint volume and resolution performance.
When complaints peak, for workforce planning.
Which regions have the highest complaint density.
An interactive dashboard to explore it all.

The flight data sits in a star-schema model with DAX measures, prepared and cleaned in Power Query.

sections.title: Make the emergency room readable.
body: Raw hospital emergency data hides the things an ER team needs at a glance: how many patients came in, how long they waited, how satisfied they were, who was admitted and where they were referred.
This dashboard turns that data into structured, actionable views for operational planning, patient experience and resource allocation.

projects.title: Virat Kohli Performance Dashboard
projects.summary: A full-stack cricket analytics app: React charts on a FastAPI API that runs live SQL aggregations over Virat Kohli's career data.

experience.label: Career explorer · rebuilt from the dataset

sections.title: A career, queried live.
body: A full-stack dashboard that analyses Virat Kohli's international career across formats, years, opponents, venues and batting positions.

The React frontend calls a FastAPI backend, which builds SQL queries from the selected filters; MySQL does the aggregation and returns fresh numbers, so every chart updates with the filters instead of showing static images.
